name: throttled-py-reversible-rate-limit-reservations
instr:
Allow callers to reserve rate-limit capacity before fallible work, then commit successful work or cancel abandoned work without charging for it. Reservations must behave consistently across synchronous and asyncio limiters while preserving existing behavior for callers that continue using ordinary limit and peek operations.

A reserve operation consumes available capacity immediately and returns a stable identity plus an accepted or limited state snapshot. Every accepted reservation has exactly one terminal outcome: matching settlements are idempotent, conflicting settlements raise `ReservationSettledError`, and commit makes the charge permanent without consuming capacity again. Cancellation reverses only that reservation's contribution while preserving later admissions across fixed-window, sliding-window, token-bucket, leaking-bucket, and GCRA limiters. Window settlement respects the reservation's original period and weighted history, bucket settlement applies elapsed refill or leakage within configured capacity, and GCRA settlement preserves later arrivals, monotonic time, and nonnegative timing values. Settlement is atomic: backend failure changes neither lifecycle nor algorithm state, so the same handle can retry safely. Reservation ownership is isolated by namespace, algorithm, key, and identity; cross-settlement raises `ReservationMismatchError` without changing either limiter. Async reservations are fully awaitable and expose the same decisions, lifecycle, race resolut
